questions.q: Planning success and duration by margin (36 frozen source queries × 5 margins = 180 requests)
questions.a: 0.90: 29/36 solved, duration p50 0.5080 s; 0.95: 29/36 solved, duration p50 0.4920 s; 0.975: 29/36 solved, duration p50 0.4903 s; 0.99: 29/36 solved, duration p50 0.4861 s; 1.00: 29/36 solved, duration p50 0.4781 s. The 7 failures are the same source queries at every margin (failure is query-, not margin-dependent); every arm therefore has the same 29 matched pairs and no differential-missingness bias. Constructed TimeOpt configuration audited on all 180 requests: only limit_scale and jerk_limit_scale differ from the pinned default.

Exact continuous-time feasibility (serialized model, physical limits; compiled producer + independent verifier)
questions.a: 0.90: 29 certified / 0 exact violations / 0 unknown; 0 need adaptive subdivision; solver's own scaled contract genuinely violated by 8; 0.95: 29 certified / 0 exact violations / 0 unknown; 0 need adaptive subdivision; solver's own scaled contract genuinely violated by 8; 0.975: 29 certified / 0 exact violations / 0 unknown; 17 need adaptive subdivision; solver's own scaled contract genuinely violated by 3; 0.99: 29 certified / 0 exact violations / 0 unknown; 28 need adaptive subdivision; solver's own scaled contract genuinely violated by 5; 1.00: 17 certified / 12 exact violations / 0 unknown; 29 need adaptive subdivision; solver's own scaled contract genuinely violated by 12. Worst physical witness at 1.00: normalized residual 0.00588. Feasibility is preserved up to 0.99 but proofs need subdivision; at 1.00, 12/29 outputs genuinely violate a physical limit between solver samples.

questions.q: Native time→progress inversion versus the exact time law
questions.a: Every float32 requested time of 224 real outputs (2.364e+11 times, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090) was executed with the pinned progress_at_time and compared with a rigorous enclosure of the exact inverse: certified max |s_native − s*| ≤ 2.44e-07; induced state shift ≤ 8e-06 (v), 8.5e-06 (a), 0.00026 (j, off-knot) of the limits. Reported values within physical limits at every float32 time on 200/224 outputs; all exceedances are scale-1.00 outputs and coincide exactly with the exact-model violation witnesses.

questions.q: Certification latency after optimization (RTX 3090, paired fresh requests)
questions.a: Added p50 12.32 ms (1 thread) → 2.04 ms (8 threads); paired Δ -10.29 ms [-10.32, -10.26]; p95 2.06 ms; pooled p99 2.36 ms. Target p95 ≤ 3 ms met; p50 ≤ 1 ms not met. Outputs identical across thread counts.

Exhaustive over all positive normal float32 inputs on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090: rcp_1_div_y ≤ 0.975 ulp, sqrtf ≤ 0.944 ulp, rsqrtf ≤ 1.514 ulp, div_by_6 ≤ 0.667 ulp; SASS shows MUFU.RCP/MUFU.SQRT/MUFU.RSQ, FFMA contraction and .FTZ, consistent with A1–A4.

questions.q: Soundness of the parallel compiled certifier
questions.a: O3: 10000 cases, 0 breaches ; O0: 10000 cases, 0 breaches ; native: 10000 cases, 0 breaches (seeded adversarial cases vs exact Fraction reference, 4 OpenMP threads per call).

decision: Paper: GO — exploratory but rigorous results: exact continuous-time violations of time-optimal outputs between samples as the planning margin is removed, adaptive proofs at ≈H0 cost, an exhaustively audited native time law and reported-value contract, and ≈2 ms complete certification. Native reported-value certification (per audited output): GO for research use, conditional on the audited compiled code path and GPU. Native physical-time certification as a qualified deployment claim: NO-GO until the per-output audit contract is reviewed independently, frozen, and run on the registered Dev40/Holdout100/Confirm300 cohorts (not run). Margin policy: no margin is recommended from these exploratory data; 0.99 kept every output feasible with ≈2.3% shorter durations, 1.00 produced genuine violations in 12/29 outputs.
